summary: Audit of tasks 4.13m-4.13p at c46161f (range a3799be..c46161f, phase_base_sha 57baaaa364f968a2f44c6e14eb96f8a9d68beebf, role_base_sha e35ccf6b966a10bf8fd87f69793ee8c47e5c4ae7 per the 4.13p row). HEAD equals the audited sha. The four planned contracts hold. (1) Every real opencode call of provider-credential.sh, review-run.sh, and judge-run.sh holds --standalone (run_seed_export, run_opencode import/scan, run_model_call), pinned by ST1-ST5. (2) The seed makes exactly one real-HOME call, auth export <provider> --standalone under timeout 60 in an empty mktemp cwd with no .git; the import and scan-values keep the job HOME; an empty shared store refuses the run with exit 2, one <runner>: line, no call, and no record, pinned failing-first by R1 and JR1. (3) The HOME guards and the daemon guard are present: stop_daemons selects only serve --service processes under the run's job root, TERM then KILL after 5 s, writes <runner>: INFRA stopped daemon <pid> on stderr only and the same text in the infra array of the pass, probe, or run record; every record write is either preceded by stop_daemons or happens before a job folder exists, and the EXIT trap covers every exit path. The INFRA line never reaches stdout, so the night driver's one-line-per-route output and the probe driver's parsing are intact. (4) Every reader of the records accepts the new field: adjudicate.ts, review-score.ts, and guide.ts parse JSON by named field and never read the runner record files, and the night driver's state= read is python json.load().get("state"), tolerant of the added field. Gates one file at a time, fakes only: review-run.test.ts all 62 named tests pass (bun); judge-run.test.ts 34 passed (34); credential-provider.test.ts 16 passed (16); after each file the pgrep scans for fake-opencod[e] and quota-serve[r] showed nothing of mine. The two suite-level failures I saw on review-run were cross-session contamination: a sibling session ran the same suite concurrently (bun test PID 468934 started 04:32:31 +07, temp tree /tmp/mg-review-run-MWG730, its decoy-D2 spawned at 04:34:02 while no suite of mine ran), and its decoy daemons, which live 120 s and are built to survive the guard, tripped my environment scans. Red 4.13o failed first on exactly the named new cases (red-4.13o.log: review-run 56 pass 6 fail D1 D2 D3 S1 S5 R1; judge-run 4 failed 30 passed JD1 JS1 JS2 JR1), so the new behavior is failing-first. The real probe ran 04:35 +07 at the audited HEAD: at my final read (04:40:55 +07) probe-4.10.txt held the header plus one correct seed-refusal line for each of the first two pilot routes (deepseek, hy4), and the third pilot route (mimo) was still mid-run with its line pending; the refusal is the correct 4.13p behavior for an empty shared store, not a defect. No blocking finding.
nonblocking_findings: N1 minor (harness/model-guide/provider-credential.sh:87-91 and :97, harness/model-guide/review-run.sh:661-664, harness/model-guide/judge-run.sh:445-448): the three new HOME-guard refusal lines (provider-credential: the call HOME is outside the job root; review-run/judge-run: the job HOME is outside the job root) have no failing-first test, and in the current wiring they cannot trip through the public interface: check_job_home is always called with $FOLDER/home, which the same script constructs (provider-credential.sh:97), and the runner guards compare $JOB/home against $JOB. They satisfy the 4.13o contract as defense-in-depth and every refusal keeps exit 2, but no test pins the lines or their exit codes; fix: pin them with a forced-guard test or note them as unreachable in the plan, no behavior change.

N2 minor (harness/model-guide-tests/review-run.test.ts:1735 and :321-324), pre-existing fragility, unchanged in this range and re-proven today: the live-process and orphan scans match any fake-opencode or quota-server command line on the machine, not only this run's temp tree, so a sibling session's fake daemons fail the gate while every named test passes; today a sibling suite (bun test PID 468934, started 04:32:31 +07, tree /tmp/mg-review-run-MWG730) left decoy children alive (sleep 120, built to survive the guard) and tripped my spawn test once and my afterAll sweep once; all 62 named tests passed both times; fix: scope the scans to the run's own temp tree, no behavior change.

N3 minor (harness/model-guide/review-run.sh:440-475, same block in judge-run.sh:335-370): stop_daemons collects the pids once and then writes one INFRA line for every pid of that list, so a daemon that exits on its own during the TERM wait still gets a stopped-daemon line naming a pid the guard did not itself stop; the operator signal (daemon gone) stays true and D1/D3/D2/JD1 pin the real kill path, so this is wording precision only; fix: write the line only for pids the guard signalled, no behavior change.
evidence: Provenance: git rev-parse HEAD -> c46161fb858de0883cf304a7dfc40f0afd486e64, equal to the audited HEAD; git diff --name-only a3799be..c46161f -> the three planned scripts (review-run.sh, judge-run.sh, provider-credential.sh), the fake-opencode fixture, the two planned test files (review-run.test.ts, judge-run.test.ts), credential-provider.test.ts (planned by Red 4.13m), and measure/tracks/model_guide/plan.md; nothing else changed.

Refusal lines and exit codes (contract 1): refuse in provider-credential.sh (lines 41-44) echoes provider-credential: <check> to stderr and exits 2; refuse in review-run.sh (122-126) and judge-run.sh (90-93) echo one <runner>: line to stdout and exit 2; the new guards call these helpers (provider-credential.sh:87-91 with the call at 97, review-run.sh:661-664, judge-run.sh:445-448); the empty-shared-store seed failure chains provider-credential: the credential seed failed (stderr, exit 2) into review-run: / judge-run: the provider credential seed failed (review-run.sh:668-670, judge-run.sh:450-452), exit 2, no call, no record, pinned by R1 (review-run.test.ts:3115) and JR1 (judge-run.test.ts:2544).

INFRA line and infra field (contract 2): stop_daemons (review-run.sh:440-475, judge-run.sh:335-370) writes <runner>: INFRA stopped daemon <pid> to stderr only (review-run.sh:470-471, judge-run.sh:365-366), and INFRA_LIST flows into the infra array of the pass record (review-run.sh:619-625), the probe record (review-run.sh:761-764), and the judge run record (judge-run.sh:750-753), added only when non-empty; every record write is preceded by stop_daemons (review-run.sh:849 before write_probe_record, review-run.sh:981 before write_record, judge-run.sh:897 before write_files) or happens before a job folder exists (review-run.sh:640-646, JOB still empty); the EXIT trap runs stop_daemons on every exit path (review-run.sh:477, judge-run.sh:372). D1, D3, D2, JD1 pin the line, the field, and the decoy survival; the decoy (HOME and cwd outside the job root) survives because daemon_pids (review-run.sh:411-448) matches only processes whose HOME or cwd is under the run's job root.

Reader coverage (contract 2): the night driver reads the pass record with python json.load(open(file)).get("state") (night-4.11.sh:181), which accepts the added field; adjudicate.ts parses only key, queue, and judge files by named field (adjudicate.ts:291,380,454) and never reads runner records; review-score.ts reads the keys, outputs, and its own score files (review-score.ts:324,329,515); guide.ts reads score files by named field (guide.ts:161-166,247-254); preview.sh reads score files (preview.sh:908-1013); all parse JSON with no exact-key validation, so the additive infra field breaks no reader.

Seed export (contract of 4.13o point 3): run_seed_export (provider-credential.sh:157-165) runs timeout 60 env -u OPENCODE_DB OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1 $OPENCODE_BIN auth export <provider> --standalone with the real HOME untouched and the cwd in an empty mktemp -d folder that is removed after the call; the import (provider-credential.sh:204) and the scan-values export (provider-credential.sh:212) keep the job HOME through run_opencode, and check_job_home runs before each such call (provider-credential.sh:97); the fake answers auth export from the shared store when HOME is the real HOME and from the job store when HOME is the job home (fake-opencode:177-183), so S1-S5 and JS1-JS2 pin the exact call inventory and R1/JR1 pin the empty-shared refusal; C3 in credential-provider.test.ts pins the no-entry refusal of the helper itself.

Gates at HEAD, one file at a time, fakes only: bun test harness/model-guide-tests/review-run.test.ts -> all 62 named tests pass (run 2: 62 pass, the only fail is the unnamed afterAll sweep tripped by a sibling's decoy); cd harness && npx vitest run model-guide-tests/judge-run.test.ts --configLoader native --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot -> Tests 34 passed (34), exit 0; cd harness && npx vitest run model-guide-tests/credential-provider.test.ts --configLoader native --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot -> Tests 16 passed (16), exit 0; after each file, pgrep -af fake-opencod[e] and pgrep -af quota-serve[r] printed nothing of mine.

Failing-first: red-4.13o.log records the Red gates before the implementation (review-run 56 pass 6 fail: D1, D2, D3, S1, S5, R1, each failing only on the missing 4.13o behavior; judge-run Tests 4 failed | 30 passed: JD1, JS1, JS2, JR1) and the Red fix 28543bd changed no production file; green-4.13p.log records the passing gates and the same refusal contract I verified in the code.

Cross-session contamination, reported with PID evidence: run 1 of review-run.test.ts (started 04:29:45 +07) failed only the spawn test's live-process scan on a stale decoy (PID 435116, fake-opencode serve --service mg-decoy-D1 120) spawned before my run began; run 2 (all 62 named tests pass) failed only the afterAll sweep on the sibling's decoy-D1 (PID 505234) while the sibling suite ran the same file (bun test PID 468934, started 04:32:31 +07, temp tree /tmp/mg-review-run-MWG730); at 04:34:02 the sibling's decoy-D2 (PID 507820, parent 468934) spawned while no suite of mine ran, proving the processes were not mine; both decoys die after 120 s and both pgrep scans after each of my runs were empty.

Driver isolation: the runner locks are per private dir (review-run.sh:501-503, judge-run.sh:579-581), my tests use temp private trees, and the daemon guard matches only processes under each run's own job root, so my test runs cannot block or stop the real 04:35 probe; the probe's stderr lines (any INFRA, the helper refusal) go to probe-4.10.log while its per-route stdout lines keep the driver's one-line format.

probe-4.10.txt (the real probe of task 4.10, run 04:35 +07 at HEAD c46161f; my final read at 04:40:55 +07): it holds the header probe-4.10 2026-11-19T04:35:00+07:00 HEAD c46161fb858de0883cf304a7dfc40f0afd486e64 dry=0 and exactly one correct line for each of the first two pilot routes: opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash refused review-run: the provider credential seed failed exit=2, and opencode/hy4-flash-free refused review-run: the provider credential seed failed exit=2. The third pilot route, opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash, was still mid-run at that read, so its line had not landed; the driver appends exactly one line per route (a refused line, a plain outcome line, or a skipped line), so the route will hold one line of the same format. The probe log shows one provider-credential: the credential seed failed stderr line per refused route and the job folder cleanup (OPENCODE_HOME CLEANUP stopped=1) after each. The real shared store of the operator HOME holds no entry for these providers, so the seed refusal is the correct 4.13p behavior at the audited HEAD, not a defect: the run stopped before any model call and wrote no record.
